headline: Sales grow but a belts impairment sinks GAAP profit
summary_short: Timken's Q2 2026 net sales rose 7.5% y/y to $1.26B (4.4% organic), but net income fell 63% y/y to $28.9M ($0.41 diluted EPS) on a $94.4M impairment tied to the pending belts-business divestiture; adjusted EPS rose 28.9% to $1.83 and adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 190bps to 19.6%.
summary_long: Sales growth was driven by higher volumes in both segments, higher pricing, the Bijur Delimon acquisition, and favorable FX; Industrial Motion sales rose 14.6% y/y (helped by Bijur Delimon) while Engineered Bearings rose 3.8%. GAAP net income fell to $28.9M as a $94.4M impairment/restructuring charge tied to the planned belts-business sale to Gates Industrial weighed on results; excluding special items, adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 190bps to 19.6% on positive price/mix and $8.0M of net tariff refunds. Free cash flow was $80.5M; net debt-to-adjusted-EBITDA held at 2.0x. Timken raised full-year 2026 guidance: GAAP EPS to $3.75-$4.05, adjusted EPS to $6.05-$6.35, and revenue growth to ~5.5% (from ~5%) at the midpoint.

drivers.explanation: Management's 'Elevate to Outperform' strategy delivered higher volumes, pricing and margin expansion in both segments; the company raised its full-year 2026 EPS, adjusted EPS, and revenue outlook, citing first-half execution and improving demand.
Growth was driven by higher volumes across both segments, higher pricing, revenue from the Bijur Delimon acquisition, and favorable FX translation.
Organic growth of 4.4% is the 7.5% reported growth net of $20.6M from the Bijur Delimon acquisition and $15.1M of favorable currency translation, per the release's own reconciliation table.
Operating income fell mainly on the $94.4M belts-business impairment/restructuring charge plus higher SG&A, partially offset by segment EBITDA growth in both segments.
Net income fell mainly on a $94.4M impairment/restructuring charge tied to the pending sale of the belts business to Gates Industrial and the closure of its Springfield, Missouri plant.

Tracks the net-income decline; per the company's own GAAP-to-adjusted reconciliation, total special items (led by the $94.4M belts impairment) reduced GAAP diluted EPS by $1.42 versus adjusted EPS this quarter.
Margin expansion of 190bps was driven by positive price/mix, higher volume, and an $8.0M net benefit from IEEPA tariff refunds, partially offset by higher operating costs in both segments.

Not explained in the release beyond the cash-flow statement's working-capital line items (e.g., accounts receivable and unbilled receivables outflows); no narrative cause is given for the y/y decline.
Free cash flow rose slightly as lower capital expenditures ($26.6M vs $33.1M a year ago) offset a modest decline in operating cash flow.
